stories.title: Kawhi Leonard Investigation — Could Drag Into 2027, Trade Still Frozen
stories.angle: ESPN reports probe could extend past season start; NBPA arbitration threat adds delay; Raptors trade in legal limbo

— Contract void

This is the wildest story in basketball. #NBA #Clippers

facebook.long_form:
⚠️ The Kawhi Leonard situation just got more complicated — and it could get a lot worse before it gets better.

ESPN is reporting that the NBA's investigation into Kawhi Leonard and the Los Angeles Clippers could now drag into 2027. The investigation centers on a reported $28 million endorsement deal between Leonard and Aspiration, an environmental company in which Clippers owner Steve Ballmer had personally invested $50 million. The allegation: this was a disguised salary payment designed to circumvent the league's salary cap.

Here's where things stand today:
— The Clippers had agreed to trade Leonard back to the Toronto Raptors before this offseason. But the moment the NBA told Toronto they would assume full financial and basketball liability for any punishment handed to Leonard upon completing the trade, both teams formally placed the transaction on hold.
— Commissioner Adam Silver has said he wants the matter resolved before the 2026-27 season begins — but if no settlement is reached, the case goes to a neutral CBA arbitrator with NO hard deadline. That's the path to 2027.
— The NBPA has made clear it will go to arbitration if the league attempts to discipline Leonard without what it considers sufficient evidence.
— The penalties on the table are severe: voiding of Leonard's contract, a player suspension, team fines up to $7.5 million, and loss of draft picks.

Meanwhile, Kawhi Leonard is set to earn $50.3 million in 2026-27 — money he's currently owed but can't even be traded while under investigation. Sanberg, one of the key figures in the Aspiration deal, has been sentenced to 14 years in prison.

The Clippers are denying all wrongdoing. The Raptors are stuck in limbo. And the league's timeline is slipping.

This is one of the most extraordinary situations in NBA history — and it's only getting stranger.

💬 What do you think should happen? Drop the investigation and let the trade go through? Void the contract? Let us know below.

LeBron. Embiid (healthy, per coaches). Brown. Maxey. Edgecombe.

facebook.long_form:
🏀 LeBron James hasn't even played a regular-season game for the Philadelphia 76ers yet — and he's already pushing his new teammates to their limits at 5 in the morning.

LeBron recently described his early-morning routine with Tyrese Maxey: "Every morning, 5 a.m., we're in the gym, 5:30, whatever in the gym, and you just see his dedication."

This is what the 76ers built this offseason. Not just a roster — a culture. LeBron (41 years old and still conducting pre-dawn workouts) and Maxey, one of the game's rising point guards, are the foundation of what could be the most star-studded team in the league.

The projected starting five: LeBron James, Joel Embiid, Jaylen Brown, Tyrese Maxey, and Jared Edgecombe — a group that collectively owns FIVE NBA MVP awards. Embiid's health was the one lingering question, and the 76ers' coaching staff has publicly confirmed Embiid is healthy and ready for Day 1 of training camp.

Camp doesn't open until late September. The preseason is expected to tip off October 8 when Philadelphia reportedly visits Brooklyn at Barclays Center.

But the real prep work? It's already happening. Every morning. At 5 AM.

💬 Is this the most talented team in the East? Or does the Knicks' championship pedigree still make them the team to beat?

#NBA #NBASchedule

facebook.long_form:
📅 The 2026-27 NBA schedule is about to drop — and if history holds, Thursday is the day.

Marc Stein reported this week that the league's schedule is "on course to be announced next week," pointing to Thursday, August 13, as the most likely reveal date. That tracks: each of the last three NBA schedule releases happened on a Thursday (Aug 14, 2025; Aug 15, 2024; Aug 17, 2023).

The hold-up? The league was waiting on LeBron James's free agency decision. Now that he's officially a Philadelphia 76er, the marquee game planners can get to work. And there is NO shortage of marquee games to build around this season:

🏆 Knicks Banner Night — Oct 20 at Madison Square Garden, where New York will raise its first championship banner in 53 years.
👑 LeBron's 76ers Opener — The league will want LeBron James in a primetime spot as early as opening night. The matchup TBD.
🇫🇷 Wembanyama's Spurs — Victor Wembanyama is entering Year 4 and just locked in a 5yr/$252M extension.
🏀 Six New Head Coaches — Dusty May (Mavs), Adrian Griffin (Bucks), Torsten Splitter (Bulls), Nate Sweeney (Magic), Willie Green (Pelicans), Micah Nori (Blazers) are all beginning new eras.

Set your calendars for Aug 13. This might be the most anticipated schedule drop in a decade.

stories.title: Curry Extension Window Opens August 29 — What Warriors Need to Know
stories.angle: Clarifying the Aug 29 eligibility date; mutual interest confirmed; lingering roster questions after LeBron chose Philadelphia

x_posts.label: Post 4
x_posts.text:
Quick fact: Stephen Curry's extension window opens August 29 — not today.

The expected deal: 2 years, $136.7M. ESPN's Anthony Slater: "mutual interest" confirmed.

He wants to finish in Golden State. The Warriors need to earn that. 💛

#Warriors #NBA

facebook.long_form:
📋 A quick clarification on the Stephen Curry extension timeline — because there's been some confusion this week.

Stephen Curry does NOT become eligible to sign his contract extension until August 29, 2026. Not today. Not this week. August 29.

When that date arrives, the Warriors are expected to offer Curry a 2-year, $136.7 million deal — roughly $68.35 million per year. That would carry him through his age-40 season and his 24th year in the NBA. ESPN's Anthony Slater has reported "mutual interest" from both sides, and those close to Curry say he wants to finish his career in Golden State.

But there's a genuine question the Warriors need to answer: can they give Curry a roster worth coming back for?

This summer brought some answers. Draymond Green re-signed on a 1-year, $27.7 million deal. Gary Payton II is back. But LeBron James chose Philadelphia — the Warriors were reportedly in the mix — and the path to a championship isn't obvious from where they currently stand.

Curry shot 42% from three last season at age 38. He's not done. He just needs the right supporting cast.

Watch August 29.

---

stories.title: Dillon Brooks Signs 3-Year, $73M Extension with Phoenix Suns
stories.angle: Veteran wing locks in long-term deal; Suns building identity around defense and physicality heading into 2026-27

x_posts.label: Post 5
x_posts.text:
Dillon Brooks. 3 years. $73 million. Phoenix Suns.

The enforcer is staying put. Phoenix is building around defense and physicality.

The West just got more physical. 💪

#Suns #NBA

facebook.long_form:
🔒 Dillon Brooks is staying in Phoenix.

The veteran defensive wing has agreed to a 3-year, $73 million extension with the Phoenix Suns, locking in one of the NBA's most physical and disruptive wing defenders for the next three seasons. The deal was confirmed in league transaction reports this week.

Brooks — known as one of the league's most aggressive on-ball defenders and an uncompromising physical presence — fits perfectly into what the Suns appear to be building. After a roster turnover-heavy offseason, Phoenix is signaling a clear identity: tough, defensive, physical.

The Suns roster still has questions around it, but Brooks at $73M over three years represents an investment in a proven culture-setter. If you're building a defensive team in the Western Conference, you want players who embrace the physical edge — and Brooks has built his entire career on it.

At $24.3 million per year, it's a fair deal for a player who brings energy and accountability to the defensive end on every single night.

---
